title: Capacity Escrow and Model Deprecation Guidelines
author: Nisha Rao
body:
Overview

Purpose: Define a cross-functional standard to retire model variants or inference features while guaranteeing customer continuity via capacity escrow, API compatibility windows, observability-driven rollback, and transparent billing adjustments. This document is the authoritative process for engineering, SRE, product, and billing teams when a model or variant is scheduled for deprecation.

Goals
- Minimize customer impact when a model variant is removed or replaced.
- Ensure predictable capacity and performance during migration windows.
- Provide clear timelines and automation for notifications, fallbacks, and rollbacks.
- Preserve billing transparency and avoid surprise charges.

Scope
- Applies to: model variants (quantized vs full-precision), custom fine-tuned artifacts, runtime feature toggles that change response fidelity, and streaming response contract changes.
- Out of scope: UI-only changes, documentation edits, or purely internal refactors with no API/behavioral impact.

Key Definitions
- Escrow Capacity: A reserved pool of serving capacity (GPU/CPU slots + KV cache quota) retained for a deprecation period to support client migration and rollback.
- Compatibility Window: The time window between deprecation announcement and enforced removal where both old and new variants are served.
- Grace Routing: Automatic routing rules that send traffic to compatible fallback variants if the preferred variant is unavailable.
- Migration Debt: The remaining percentage of active clients still using the deprecated variant.

Principles
1. Safe, observable deprecation: every deprecation must be announced, monitored, and reversible during the compatibility window.
2. Cost-bounded escrow: escrow capacity must be sized to balance customer continuity with economic constraints; SRE approves oversubscription policy.
3. Opt-in auto-migration first: where possible, clients should be auto-migrated to a compatible variant with the same output schema and SLOs.
4. Transparent billing: customers receive a deprecation notice that includes any temporary billing adjustments or credits.

Standards and Requirements
- Minimum compatibility window: 30 days for public hosted API; 60 days for Dedicated/Private customers unless contract specifies otherwise.
- Escrow capacity sizing algorithm (high level): reserve max(5% of baseline fleet, 1 p95 client ramp) or explicit runbook estimate from product + SRE.
- Observability coverage: at least the following signals must be instrumented prior to announcement:
  - per-tenant variant usage (% of requests)
  - error rate delta (5xx and model-output validation)
  - latency p50/p95/p99 per variant
  - migration debt trend (daily)

Escrow Capacity Table (example sizing guidance)
| Customer Class | Typical Baseline | Escrow Reserve Minimum | Comments |
|---------------|------------------:|-----------------------:|---------|
| Self-serve / Small | <= 5k req/day | 5% baseline or 5 concurrent slots | Auto-migrate preferred |
| Mid-market | 5k–200k req/day | 3–10 GPU-minutes equivalent | Coordinate with SE |
| Enterprise / Dedicated | >200k req/day | Negotiated reserve (SLA-backed) | Contract-led

Operational Runbook (step-by-step)
1) Pre-announcement (owner: product + runtime owner)
   a) Validate that the new variant meets compatibility tests: schema, example prompt regressions, rate-limited synthetic tests.
   b) Determine escrow size and duration; publish in deprecation proposal.
   c) Configure observability dashboard and synthetic alerts (see metrics below).

2) Announcement (owner: product comms)
   a) Publish deprecation notice to customers: API email, console banner, FAQ. Include compatibility window, migration options, and billing changes.
   b) Create internal change ticket with rollout timeline and owners.

3) Migration period (owner: runtime + SRE)
   a) Enable Grace Routing with explicit fallback map: {deprecated_variant -> preferred_variants_ordered}.
   b) Start automatic soft-redirects for opt-in customers; record migration metrics per tenant.
   c) Monitor Migration Debt and per-tenant error deltas. If Migration Debt > 80% at day 20, escalate to product + CSM.

4) Final enforcement (owner: runtime)
   a) Disable writes/creates for the deprecated variant at the end of compatibility window.
   b) Continue escrow capacity for 72 hours post-enforcement for emergency rollback.
   c) If rollback is necessary, execute the rollback play in the rollback checklist.

5) Post-deprecation (owner: SRE + billing)
   a) Reclaim escrow capacity in phases; update cost accounting.
   b) Issue pro-rated billing adjustments or credits as published.
   c) Archive variant artifacts and record provenance in model manifest.

Metrics and Alerts (required)
- Per-variant 5xx rate > baseline + 0.5% for 10 minutes -> P1 on-call alert.
- Migration debt drop rate < 2% per day after day 7 -> page SRE and product.
- New-variant regression (quality eval set) > defined threshold -> fail migration and halt auto-migration.

API and Client Contract Requirements
- Deprecation header: All responses for deprecated variants must include the header X-Model-Deprecation: variant=<name>;deadline=<YYYY-MM-DD>;migration_url=<link> during the compatibility window.
- Deprecation notice payload (example JSON)
{
  "variant": "redwood-small-quant-2024-09",
  "deadline": "2026-03-20",
  "migration_options": ["redwood-small-2025-12", "redwood-small-quant-2025"],
  "support_contact": "support@redwood.ai",
  "escrow_capacity_minutes": "720"
}
- Clients must gracefully accept 429/503 with Retry-After when grace routing enacts temporary throttles.

CLI and Automation Examples
- Create deprecation notice (runtime-admin CLI):
  redwood-admin deprecate-variant --variant redwood-small-quant-2024-09 --deadline 2026-03-20 --escrow-minutes 720 --notify-owners

- Query migration debt per tenant (example SQL):
  SELECT tenant_id, SUM(case when variant = 'redwood-small-quant-2024-09' then 1 else 0 end)/SUM(1) as debt FROM requests WHERE time > now()-interval '30 days' GROUP BY tenant_id;

Rollback Checklist
1. Open emergency channel and notify stakeholders.
2. Re-enable deprecated variant in routing and validate health checks.
3. Restore previous escrow allocation and remove any hard enforcement gates.
4. Capture forensics: diff of request/response anomalies and deployment artifacts.
5. Plan next steps: extend compatibility window or provide mitigation path.

Ownership and Approval Matrix
- Product: approves migration UX, customer communication text, and compatibility window length.
- Runtime Owner: sizes escrow capacity, implements grace routing and enforcement hooks.
- SRE: approves observability coverage and escalation thresholds.
- Billing: defines and approves any temporary charge adjustments and credits.
- Legal/Compliance: reviews for enterprise contracts or regulatory customers.

FAQ and Edge Cases
Q: What if a deprecated variant has unique behavior that cannot be emulated?
A: Treat as a breaking deprecation: extend compatibility window and coordinate one-on-one migrations; no auto-migration.

Q: Can escrow capacity be billed back to the owning product?
A: Yes — by default product teams absorb escrow cost center; for enterprise customers, negotiate in contract.

Audit and Evidence
- Every deprecation must be logged with the following artifacts (stored in the deprecation ticket): announcement copy, escrow sizing rationale, observability dashboard links, migration debt reports, billing adjustment records, and final forensic notes.

Appendix: Example Dashboard Panels
- Variant Usage Heatmap (per-tenant)
- Migration Debt Over Time (stacked by tenant)
- Error Delta by Variant (p50/p95 latency + 5xx)
- Escrow Utilization (GPU-minutes)

Appendix: Quick Compatibility Tests (automation)
1) Contract test: validate output JSON schema with existing schema validator.
2) Regression test: run 100 synthetic prompts from the regression suite; require >= 95% pass on acceptance criteria.
3) Load smoke: run 1-minute ramp to 2x expected baseline against escrowed pool; check p95 latency within SLO.
